intro.title: Build tracing instrumentation for requests
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple tracing instrumentation system to monitor HTTP requests in a Node.js application. You will learn how to generate unique trace IDs for each incoming request and log them along with the request method and URL. The core programming concept involves using middleware functions to intercept and augment requests in an Express.js server. You will work with key Node.js constructs like the crypto module for ID generation and console logging for output. By the end, you will understand how tracing helps in debugging and observing application flow in real-time.
intro.usecase: Tracing instrumentation is essential for monitoring and debugging distributed systems in production. Developers implement request tracing in microservices architectures to track user journeys across multiple services, such as an e-commerce checkout flow spanning authentication, inventory, and payment APIs. This enables teams to visualize performance bottlenecks in observability dashboards like Grafana or Jaeger, helping them quickly diagnose latency issues and improve user experience. In real-world applications, this pattern is used by companies like Netflix and Uber to ensure reliability and maintain service-level agreements (SLAs) for critical user-facing features.
